from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 2x2 Case: Geometric Calculation", [
            "For 2x2 matrices, calculate ad minus bc.", 
            "This value defines the parallelogram's area.", 
            "Vectors span the transformed area in space."
        ])
        
        # Define base vectors
        a, b, c, d = 2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.5
        v1 = np.array([a, c, 0])
        v2 = np.array([b, d, 0])
        
        vec1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, v1, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        vec2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, v2, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        
        # Parallelogram
        poly = Polygon(ORIGIN, v1, v1+v2, v2, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # Position objects using grid
        # Group them to place centrally in the right quadrant
        group = VGroup(vec1, vec2, poly)
        self.place_at_grid(group, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        formula = MathTex("Area = ad - bc", font_size=36, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(vec1), Create(vec2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(poly))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The sign shows the orientation of space.", "Positive determinant means original orientation is preserved.", "Negative means the space has been mirrored."]
        self.setup_layout("The Sign Significance: Orientation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects
        arrow_preserved = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=RED)
        arrow_flipped = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT, color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(arrow_preserved, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(arrow_preserved))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        det_label = Text("det > 0", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(det_label, 'B2')
        self.play(Write(det_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Transform(arrow_preserved, arrow_flipped))
        det_label_neg = Text("det < 0", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(det_label_neg, 'E2')
        self.play(Write(det_label_neg))
        self.play(FadeOut(det_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Singularity: When the Area Collapses", [
            "Zero determinant means the area collapses.",
            "Transformation squashes dimensions, losing all information.",
            "Such matrices are non-invertible."
        ])
        
        # Grid setup for objects
        square = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(square, 'B2', 'E5')
        self.add(square)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        # Squash into a line
        self.play(square.animate.stretch(0, 0), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Indicate zero area
        area_label = Text("Area = 0", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(area_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        label = Text("Non-invertible", font_size=24, color="#808080")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        # Fade everything out to show loss of info
        self.play(FadeOut(square), FadeOut(area_label), FadeOut(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", [
            "Determinants measure scaling and reveal orientation.",
            "They help identify invertible matrix transformations.",
            "Essential for math and computer graphics."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Recap key formulas, highlight in #00FF00
        formula = MathTex(r"det(A) = ad - bc", color=WHITE)

        self.play(formula.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show example application, color shift #00FFFF
        matrix_demo = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Square(side_length=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.3)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_demo, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), FadeIn(matrix_demo))
        self.play(matrix_demo.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final exit transition with logo #FFFFFF
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a determinant as a 'scaling factor' for area/volume during a linear transformation. Prerequisite: Students should understand vectors as arrows and matrices as functions that move those arrows.
sections.example: Visualize a unit square with a cute cat icon inside. When the matrix transforms the space, the square stretches into a parallelogram. The determinant is the ratio of the new area to the original area.

sections.title: The 2x2 Case: Geometric Calculation
sections.content: Define the determinant for a 2x2 matrix using the cross-multiplication formula (ad-bc). Relate this directly to the area of a parallelogram spanned by two column vectors.
sections.example: Matrix [[a, b], [c, d]]. Show an animation where the vectors (a, c) and (b, d) form a parallelogram. The value 'ad-bc' represents the signed area.

sections.title: The Sign Significance: Orientation
sections.content: Explain that the sign of the determinant indicates orientation. A positive sign means the 'handedness' is preserved; a negative sign means the space has been flipped (mirrored).
sections.example: Show a robot character on a screen. If the determinant is negative, the robot appears in a mirror reflection, effectively swapping its left and right.

sections.title: Singularity: When the Area Collapses
sections.content: Discuss the special case where the determinant is zero. This happens when the transformation squashes the space into a line or a point, losing dimensionality.
sections.example: An animation of a 3D cube being flattened into a flat 2D 'pancake'. When the volume becomes zero, the information is lost, and the matrix is 'non-invertible'.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge: Determinant measures scaling, indicates orientation, and identifies invertibility. Essential for solving systems of equations and computer graphics.
sections.example: A quick montage of a video game character changing size/perspective, controlled by determinant calculations in the engine's background math.
